title: Hyperscene (open canvas)
description: Generic data-driven composition — the JSON is the video. Layers (text/image/component/rect) with timed windows, kinetic splits, the cut kit (whip/punch/iris/...), WebGL shader stings (flash/burn/leak/grain/dissolve), theme bg-preset windows on canvas, global camera, captions.
note: data.theme drives palette/fonts/bg colours. Coordinates are px in the chosen orientation space (1080×1920 portrait, 1920×1080 landscape).

aspect.label: Canvas aspect (overrides orientation). CLI --aspect a,b,c renders multiple in one pass.

destination.label: Where this ships. Decides the safe area: a phone feed paints chrome over the frame, a website does not. Default web (margin only).

fps.label: Frame rate (default 30; use 60 for smoother fast motion)

captionStyle.label: Word-timed caption treatment on the pop layout (core/captions.js). Optional per-line words:[{t0,t1}].

bg.label: Background windows (canvas, theme palette)
bg.hint: the backdrop is the largest area of the frame, so the engine will not pick it for you. Use `"bg": [{ "preset": "plain" }]` for a deliberately flat field, a living preset (dotmatrix · gradientWash · blobs · metallic · metallicSheen · aurora · …), or `{ "html": "…" }` to hand-author one. See docs backgrounds-and-images.

html.label: Hand-authored living background (raw HTML/CSS instead of a preset)

tone.label: Is the hand-authored backdrop light or dark? (picks the default text ink)

opts.label: Per-video tuning of THIS preset's fx. Meta knobs scale what the preset baked in: { intensity, dotAlpha, drift, grain }. Every other key is passed straight to the fx that reads it, so the fx's own parameters work by name (liquid: scale, speed, warp, edge0, edge1, gloss, res · dots: spacing, period, k, driftX, driftY · metallic: count, waves, glow, sweep · particles: count, speed, connectDist). A key this preset's fx do not read is an ERROR, and the message lists the ones they do.

seed.label: Vary the preset's positions/phase (default = hash of theme+preset, so brands differ)

use.label: use:"theme" → pull the brand’s own authored backdrop (themes/<name>.json bgDefault)

cuts.label: Hard cuts between beats (timing x presentation, from core/cuts.js)

dist.label: Travel distance in px for a directional cut

color.label: Tint hex (recolours the effect; omit for native colours)

colors.label: leak: up to 4 hex colours the leak is built from (seed only arranges them)

seams.label: Two-scene shader transitions (blend the beats either side of a boundary, from core/seams.js)

t.label: Seam start time (s) — the window is [t, t+dur]

fx.label: Transition (samples BOTH beats as textures). Basics: fade · dissolve · slide · push · uncover · wipe (dir-aware). Expressive: crossWarp · whipPan · sdfIris · dispersion · lens · flashWhite · cinematicZoom · portal.

timing.label: Easing of the transition progress (default smooth = ease-in-out). linear = constant-speed (mechanical); smooth/out/snappy/pop/rush/brake/ramp shape the blend's velocity. Same curves as a scene cut's timing (core/cuts.js).

produced.label: Set false to OPT OUT of the produced baseline the engine injects by default (core/produce.js): a living/brand-appropriate background, a gentle camera push, and sceneUnits on cut films. Additive only (never rewrites your layers). Absent = produced (rich by default); false = render exactly what the JSON declares. Any field you set explicitly (bg, cameraMove, sceneUnits) already overrides its part of the baseline.

sceneUnits.label: Make `cuts` move each BEAT as a WHOLE UNIT (the outgoing beat slides/pushes out while the incoming slides in, as separate scenes) instead of transforming the whole camera at once. Turns beat boundaries from a per-layer-fade slideshow into real scene swaps. Beats are the intervals between cut times; layers are grouped by their start. Opt-in; a scene without it renders byte-identical. See core/cuts.js PRESENTATIONS for the styles.

transitions.label: UNIFIED transitions (one surface): a boundary transition between two beats. `fx` routes to the right mechanism automatically (cut · seam · sting) via core/transitions.js — ambiguous basics (fade/slide/wipe) default to a cheap root cut; `mech:"seam"` upgrades to the real two-scene blend. Lowered to cuts/stings/seams at load. Inventory: `make transitions`.

at.label: Boundary time (s) — the transition plays over [at, at+dur]

fx.label: Transition name (any from `make transitions`). Routed by mechanism: whipPan/crossWarp/cinematicZoom → seam; whip/punch/zoom → cut; glitch/chromaticSplit → sting; fade/slide/wipe/dissolve → cut by default (add mech:"seam" for the two-scene blend).

mech.label: Force the mechanism (default = auto). seam = two-scene GPU blend; cut = transform the scene root; sting = generative overlay.

timing.label: Easing of the transition progress (default smooth = ease-in-out; linear = constant). Same curves as a cut/seam timing.

cameraMove.label: Author sugar: { move, ...params } (or an array of them) → data.camera at expand time. Moves: slowPush | diveIn | panFollow | workspaceZoomOut | orbit | multiPhase (core/camera-moves.js).

lighting.label: The scene's KEY LIGHT: { x, y } in canvas px, plus optional { intensity } (default 1, scales every shadow at once). Read by the `shadow` modifier, which points each layer's shadow directly away from this point — so two cards either side of it throw their shadows in opposite directions, and one number re-lights the whole film. A light outside the canvas is normal.

intensity.label: Multiplies every shadow's opacity (default 1). 0 puts the lights out.

s.label: Where the camera stands, as the magnification of the canvas plane (1 = the default distance, 1.4 = closer). This is the camera's DEPTH, not a scale of the picture: with anything tilted in frame it dollies, so vanishing points move. There is deliberately no separate z key.

ease.label: Easing INTO this keyframe (default easeInOutCubic). Use "linear" on interior keyframes for a velocity-continuous multi-keyframe push (a chained ease-in-out pulses/shakes because it zeroes velocity at each keyframe).

roll.label: Camera roll about the view axis, degrees. Turns the whole frame without flattening anything tilted inside it.

p.label: The LENS: focal distance in px (default 1600; lower = wider). Not the camera's position — that is s. Keying both at once is the dolly zoom.

aspects.label: Per-aspect overrides for this camera keyframe

shader.label: shader: ambient WebGL look. Fields BEHIND content: flow/aurora/plasma/drift/mist/matrixDecode. Overlay looks ON TOP (high track, intensity 0.6-0.9): vhs/crt/filmGrain/lightLeak + barrel/heatShimmer/ripple/kaleidoscope. Tune with speed · intensity · colors · seed

html.label: html: raw hand-authored HTML/CSS for the layer (static; <script> stripped)

speed.label: clip: playback rate multiplier (1 = realtime; 0.5 = half speed)

typing.label: text: type it out at N chars/sec (true = 24) with a blinking caret

caret.label: typing: show the blinking caret (default true)

caretHold.label: typing: keep the caret after the text finishes

untype.label: typing: seconds into the layer at which the text starts DELETING backwards (backspace). Omit for forward-only typing.

untypeRate.label: untype: delete speed in chars/sec (default = the `typing` rate)

path.label: cursor: [{t,x,y,ease}] keyframes the pointer follows (x,y = absolute screen px when no layer x/y is set; relative to x/y if it is)

clicks.label: cursor: [t, …] local times to fire a click (dip + ripple)

filename.label: doc: filename shown in the card header (e.g. creed.md)

diff.label: doc: diff chip in the header (e.g. +18 -0)

blocks.label: doc: content blocks — {h,accent} heading · {body} mono lines · {code} · {bullets:[]}

bodySize.label: doc: body / code / bullet font px (default 30)

blockGap.label: doc: vertical gap above each heading block (default 22)

x.label: Left: px number, or relative "50%" / "50%-40" / center / left / right (resolved per aspect)

y.label: Top: px number, or relative "50%" / center / top / bottom (resolved per aspect)

w.label: Width: px number or "50%" of canvas

h.label: Height: px number or "50%" of canvas

pin.label: Canvas-relative placement: edge/center (center = optical), or a rule-of-thirds power point

col.label: 12-col grid placement: "3" (one column) or "2-7" (a span) → sets x + w

gutter.label: Grid gutter px (default = half the safe inset)

ls.label: Letter-spacing (e.g. "-0.03em"); unset = auto optical tracking by size

raw.label: Opt out of the micro-typography pass (tracking/balance/kerning)

italic.label: Force italic on/off (default: serif is italic, others upright). italic:false = upright serif.

size.label: Font size (px). Up to 560 for frame-filling hero words (real launch films let a single word bleed the frame — scale contrast). The auto-fit safety + `make audit` still catch true overflow/clipping.

color.label: Glow color / text color (glow accepts true = the theme accent glow)

emColor.label: <b> emphasis colour (default: brand accent, or inherit over an accent bg)

fit.label: Auto-size text down to fit w

transition.label: UNIFIED layer transition (sugar over anim/out): { in, out, dir, dur }. Lowered to anim/out/dir/enterDur/exitDur at load. `in`/`out` are anim names (core/clips.js); a raw anim/out you also set wins.

dir.label: Travel direction where the anim reads one

anim.label: Enter anim. EXACT names (core/clips.js ANIM): fade | up | rise | pop | scale | lift | defocus | slide-left | slide-right | slide-up | slide-down | wipe | wipe-left | wipe-right | wipe-up | wipe-down | iris | clock | none. Unknown names fall back to fade silently — there is no 'slide', and direction is part of the name, not a separate prop. A slide is named for the edge it comes FROM; a wipe is named for the edge its reveal TRAVELS TOWARD (wipe-up grows upward from the bottom; plain `wipe` = `wipe-right`).

out.label: driveClips exit anim. `out` plays an entrance BACKWARDS, so the exit that CONTINUES the travel is the oppositely named one: anim:"slide-right" + out:"slide-left", anim:"wipe-right" + out:"wipe-left".

split.label: Kinetic split ('path' = SVG strokes, for the `draw` preset)

preset.label: Kinetic preset (split text; incl. chroma/swing/unfold) OR glow preset (bloom/halation/diffusion/rimLight/spotlight/chromatic/chromaCycle on a glow layer)

morph.label: text layer TextMorph: letters migrate `text`->word { to, dur, ease } (needs w+align:center, GSAP). svg layer shape-morph: one path melts into another { to, dur, spin, points, closed }.

fx.label: Named GSAP effect(s) from core/gsap-effects.js: popIn | {name,dur,ease} | [blurIn,float]. Entrances (popIn/elasticIn/blurIn/spinIn/flipInX/bounceIn/clipUp/maskReveal/revealUp/expandIn/tiltIn/driftIn/glitchIn/foldIn), per-letter text (charFold/charTilt/charBlurCascade/charOvershoot, on split layers), loops (float/pulse/breathe/wobble). Pair with anim:none.

fxOut.label: Named GSAP EXIT from core/gsap-effects.js, anchored to the layer's end: fadeOut | fadeOutUp | flyOutLeft | popOut | zoomOut | blurOut | dropOut | collapseOut | spinOut | {name,dur,ease}. Mutually exclusive with `out`.

modifiers.label: Modifier stack applied to this layer, in array order, after every motion track: [{ "mixBlend": "difference" }]. Each key names a modifier from core/fx; an unknown name is a hard error, never a no-op. NOT `fx`, which is the named-GSAP-effect slot.

mixBlend.label: How this layer's pixels combine with what is painted behind it: "difference" or { mode: "difference" }. Refused on a group child: CSS blends against the nearest stacking context, which is the group, so it would reach nothing behind the group. Put it on the group.

shadow.label: Cast a shadow AWAY from the scene's `lighting`, so two layers either side of the light throw their shadows in opposite directions: 30 (px of throw) or { dist, blur, spread, color, opacity }. `color` defaults to "auto" (read off the backdrop at t: the theme's ink over a light field, black over a dark one, the accent over an accent field) and also accepts a PALETTE ROLE name ("accent", "ink") so the shadow moves with the brand. Needs a top-level `lighting`; follows the layer's BOX, not its glyphs. Refuses alongside `elevation`/`shadow`/`glow` (they write the same property). Works on a group child, whose box is measured once at build and composed with its group's; the exception is a group whose motion track keys `w`/`h`, which reflows its children.

occlude.label: Hide this layer where another layer's box covers it: "cardId" or { by: "cardId" | [ids] | "above" | "below", pad: px grown around the occluder, invert: show ONLY the overlap }. "above"/"below" mean every layer painted in front of / behind this one, read from the scene's paint order, so the set is never a hand-written list that rots when a layer is added. The hole tracks the occluder's motion track (position, scale, rotation) and closes while it is outside its own window. Needs an `id` on this layer. Works on a group child; the exception is a group whose motion track keys `w`/`h`, which reflows its children and makes their measured offsets stale.

progress.label: Write the FILM's progress (0 at the first frame, 1 at the last) into a CSS custom property this layer's markup draws with: true (writes --film), "--bar", or { var, ease }. Not `vars`, which runs over the LAYER's own window; this is the scene's clock, so a runtime bar or a chapter dot re-times itself when the film is re-cut.

kick.label: Kick this layer on the film's own joints: true, or { on: "cut" | "seam" | "sting" | "any" | [kinds], scale: multiplier (default 1.06), frames: settle length in FRAMES (default 5) }. The times come from the scene's own cuts/seams/stings, so moving a cut re-times every kick in the film. Named `kick` because `punch` is already a whole-frame CUT STYLE.

tilt.label: Turn the layer out of the picture plane: { x, y, z } degrees about its own centre, projected through ONE camera shared by every tilted layer with the same parent. { dist } px is that camera's distance (default 1600, smaller = wider lens); { origin } is its vanishing point, "center" or [x, y] in canvas px. Siblings must agree on dist/origin or it is a hard error. On a group child the camera belongs to the group, not the canvas.

motionPath.label: Fly the layer along an SVG path (GSAP MotionPathPlugin): { path:'M0,0 C...', align, autoRotate, curviness, dur, ease }. Deterministic (closed-form position per frame).

physics.label: Velocity/gravity/friction scatter (GSAP Physics2DPlugin): { velocity, angle, gravity, friction, spread, dur }. On a split layer each letter gets an index-based angle spread (explode outward). Deterministic (no random).

parts.label: Dense per-CHILD choreography: stagger a named entrance across this layer's child elements (a bespoke SVG's bars/dots/paths, a group's cards) so a figure animates piece by piece. One spec { select, anim: growUp|widen|popIn|fadeUp|riseIn|drawOn, each, stagger, delay, ease } OR an array of them (bars, then line, then dots). Pure (seeked GSAP).

comp.label: Composition name (type:"composition") — a FIRST-PARTY hand-authored per-beat GSAP timeline from core/compositions/index.js (the safe form of another engine' one-timeline-per-beat model). The JSON names the comp + passes DATA via `props`; the code lives first-party, so untrusted input cannot inject. Use for bespoke multi-tween motion `parts`/blueprints can't reach (a token travelling a path while a check draws). e.g. "pipelineFlow".

props.label: DATA passed to a `composition` comp (labels, numbers, accent) — treated as textContent/attr, never markup. e.g. { stages:["Input","Engine","Render"] }.

splitText.label: Masked LINE reveals (GSAP SplitText): { mask, stagger, dur, ease } — each line slides up from behind a clip. Line-level only; use `split` for char/word. Do not combine with `split`.

circle.label: Lay the text CHARS on a rotating circular path (badge/seal). { radius: px, period: s/turn }. Set w = 2*radius so pin centres it.

phaseStep.label: Per-unit phase offset for looping presets (wave/shimmerWave); ~0.12 = a crest travels the word

ransom.label: Comic/ransom cutout: each glyph a different face, paper swatch + torn edge (implies split:char; pair with fall/bounce). Object form: { palette: 'paper'|'color', sprites, accent, faces, swatches, cycle, stagger }. `sprites:true` uses REAL cut-out letter photos baked by `make ransom-sprites` instead of CSS tiles. `cycle` (s) re-rolls each letter into a different cutout of the SAME glyph in place

ransomSeed.label: Seed for the ransom cutout choices (defaults to the text, so the same word looks the same)

presetOpts.label: Per-preset knobs (e.g. gradient c1/c2, highlight color, blur px, tilt deg, wave amp, spring bounce/settle)

gradient.label: STATIC gradient text fill via background-clip (distinct from preset:"gradient" which sweeps): { from, to, angle? }. angle 180 = top→bottom (a dark-top→light-bottom hero word). e.g. {"from":"#1c1613","to":"#f3763b","angle":180}

lookOpts.label: Composite-look knobs (core/looks.js): color · color2 · strength (0..1 master dial) · grain · vignette · warmth. Defaults reskin to the theme.

filter.label: CSS filter string OR a named grade preset (duotone/tritone/gradientMap/posterize/sepia/vignette, or chromaGlow) OR a composite LOOK (neon/dreamyHaze/vhs/crt/filmNoir/cyberpunk/thermal/lomo/… core/looks.js). One positional arg = strength 0..1 (e.g. "neon:0.9"); full knobs via lookOpts

becomes.label: Declare that this layer CONTINUES as another (by its `id`) across a boundary. A cut transforms one root and a seam blends two frozen stills; neither joins the CONTENT, so the only thing that truly connects two scenes is a form that persists. The named layer opens on THIS layer's final pose (centres matched, size matched by scale, rotation carried) and then animates away into its own geometry, so the handover is exact by construction instead of hand-aligned and hoped for. `becomesDur` (default 0.42) and `becomesEase` shape the handover. validate fails if the two do not meet at the boundary. See docs/CRAFT/KEYED-MOTION.md.

becomesDur.label: Seconds the incoming layer takes to settle from the handed-over pose into its own (default 0.42).

becomesEase.label: Easing for the handover settle (default easeOutCubic).

panWith.label: Share another layer's motion track by its `id`, on the SAME wall clock, from THIS layer's own origin. A pan of the page is not a camera move (a camera transforms the whole frame, scrim included), so moving a surface means moving its layers together. Copied as deltas and time-shifted by the difference in `start`, so each layer keeps its own position. Anything this layer declares WINS: state your own key at a shared time to peel away from the pan, and any key at a time the pan does not cover is kept. Worked example and the reasoning: docs/CRAFT/KEYED-MOTION.md.

follow.label: Pin this layer to another layer's LIVE box, every frame: { id, edge, gap, dx, dy }. `anchor` places against the canvas and `becomes` hands one pose to another, and both resolve ONCE at build against numbers; neither can keep a label under a card that is moving, because the card's position after its motion track is only known at t. edge is center (default) · above · below · left · right, and `gap` is the space outside that edge. Centres are matched, not corners. The pin lands BEFORE this layer's own motion track, so the follower may still have choreography of its own and it plays about the pinned position. This layer needs an `id` (it is placed by its own measured size). Following a layer that is itself following a third pins you to the middle one's UNPINNED position.

acrossBeats.label: This layer belongs to the FILM, not to one beat. Only meaningful under `sceneUnits`, where every other layer is wrapped with its beat and truncated at that beat's cut. Set true and the layer attaches flat to the camera instead, keeping its authored duration and its own exit, so it can survive a cut and change across it. This is how you author a continuous object in a cut film. It paints ABOVE beat content by default (its z-index is `track` or its array index, against wrappers at auto); give it `"track": -1` to sit behind.

edgeFade.label: Image: fade the LEFT+RIGHT edges into the bg (white by default). true or fade-width %

edgeFadeColor.label: Image: colour the edgeFade dissolves into (default #ffffff; set to the bg for dark scenes)

canvasFx.label: Image: Tier-2 Canvas pass baked once at build (deterministic). Name (halftone/dither/mosaic/pixelSort/stipple/ascii/edgeDetect/crosshatch) or { fx, cell, ink, paper, seed }. core/canvas-fx.js

unit.label: Count unit appended after the number (e.g. %, k, $B); raw ≥1e6 auto-compacts (2.5B) when no unit

anchor.label: Position relative to layer with this id

pad.label: Padding (px or CSS string) — groups and text chips

children.label: Group children — text/image/count, or a nested group (layout by flow)

type.label: Child type. addGroupChild delegates to kit.buildLeaf, which dispatches the SAME layer registry as a top-level layer, so a child may be any layer type.

x.label: Child x inside a `free` group (ignored by flow layouts)

y.label: Child y inside a `free` group (ignored by flow layouts)

delay.label: Stagger this child's entrance N seconds into the group's window

layout.label: Group layout: row | column | grid | free (children place themselves at x/y)

colw.label: Grid column width in px (layout:grid; default 1fr)

fitH.label: Max height (px) for multi-line auto-fit (with fit+w) — binary-search font to fit

maxLines.label: Auto-fit safety: shrink a headline that wraps past this many lines (default 5)

items.label: align-items for a group (flex/grid): flex-start | center | flex-end | stretch | baseline

motion.label: Keyframe track — element choreography (pure in t). Offsets on the base position.

w.label: Width (px) at this key. The layer's BOX, not a scale: content re-fits instead of magnifying, which is how a sidebar collapses or a grid reflows. Needs a base `w` on the layer; state it on one key and every key inherits it.

h.label: Height (px) at this key. Same rule as `w`.

track.label: Z-order at this key. Depth over TIME: key it across a neighbour's track and the layer passes behind that neighbour and out again, which is how a ribbon orbits the thing it circles. Rounded to an integer when applied. Defaults to the layer's own `track`, or its index.

motionBlur.label: Velocity motion blur on this layer's motion track (streak on fast moves; crisp when settled). true = half-shutter; a 0..1 number sets strength. Needs a motion track.

elevation.label: Physical depth 1–4 (ring + lit edge + stacked shadows)

glow.label: Ambient glow: hex color, or true for theme accent

intensity.label: Effect strength: glow opacity (0.05-0.6) · shader visibility (up to 1)

mode.label: beam layer: 'border' (a light travelling the border) or 'shine' (a sheen sweep)

thickness.label: beam layer: border-beam ring thickness in px

period.label: beam layer (shine): seconds per sheen sweep

viewBox.label: svg layer: the path coordinate system (default '0 0 100 100')

d.label: svg layer: the path `d` string (the from-shape when morphing)

fill.label: svg layer: fill colour (default var(--accent); 'none' for draw-on)

stroke.label: svg layer: stroke colour (default var(--accent) for draw-on)

strokeWidth.label: svg layer: stroke thickness in viewBox units. Works on any stroked path, not just a draw-on one (`draw.weight` still wins when both are set).

draw.label: svg layer: stroke draws itself on. {dur, weight}

pulse.label: glow: gentle breathing, sine period in seconds (amplitude <= 0.15; off by default)

flash.label: glow: one-shot attack-decay bloom. true, or {attack,decay,peak} seconds/peak<=0.45

length.label: paint meteor: streak length in px

angle.label: glow spotlight: beam direction in degrees (0 = up, clockwise; default 150 = from above-left)

cycle.label: glow chromaCycle: seconds for the hue to sweep the full spectrum (default 6)

logotype.label: Text is part of a logo/brand mark — exempt from the CONTRAST bar only (WCAG 1.4.3)

keyClicks.label: Set false to silence the per-character key clicks a `typing` layer emits

keyGain.label: Gain of the per-character key click (default 0.3)

keyCue.label: Which cue a `typing` layer clicks with (default 'key')

aspects.label: Per-aspect overrides: { "9:16": { …props… } } merged over this layer at that canvas only

react.label: Audio react: { band:'low'|'mid'|'high', prop:'scale'|'opacity'|'blur', range:[lo,hi] } — needs audio.spectrum

vars.label: Animate CSS custom properties over the layer's window: { "--p": [from, to] }

varsDelay.label: Seconds into the layer before the `vars` sweep starts

glass.label: Frosted glass: blur what is BEHIND this layer. true = default, a number = blur px, a string = raw backdrop-filter

progressiveBlur.label: Directional blur fog on the backdrop that ramps toward an edge. { dir: top|bottom|left|right, layers: 2-12, max: px }. Fades a dense grid/list into an edge.

borderTrail.label: A glowing arc orbiting the layer border. { color, width: px, period: s/orbit, arc: deg }. CTA/end-card emphasis.

resample.label: LAYER AS TEXTURE: re-sample this layer's own pixels through a shader. Raster layers only (image/paint/shader). String, or {fx, amount, speed, seed}. amount may be [from,to] to animate.

raymarch.label: raymarch: a lit 3D subject rendered by a distance field (no geometry, no 3D engine). Give it a box the size the object should occupy; its surround is transparent. Dials: colors, intensity, speed (subject), spin (camera orbit), seed.

spin.label: raymarch: camera orbit speed (0 holds the camera still while the subject moves)

seed.label: Deterministic seed for generative layers (shader / paint / raymarch)

colors.label: Palette for a generative layer (shader / raymarch), as hex strings

opacity.label: Base opacity for the layer's whole life, multiplied into the enter/exit fade

three.label: three: a real 3D scene (geometry, materials, lights, camera). For what an SDF cannot express: a device body with captured UI on its screen, extruded type from the real brand font, UI planes in depth, a point cloud. Posed absolutely from t, so it stays pure in n.

screen.label: three deviceShowcase: image src mapped onto the device screen

planes.label: three uiParallax: image srcs or {src,x,y,z} placed in depth

travel.label: three uiParallax: how far the camera dollies over the layer's window

pointSize.label: three pointCloud: point size in world units

grain.label: Opt in to the in-engine canvas grain (default off, matching the ffmpeg pass)

audio.label: Sound. Every film should have some, and silence should be a decision you write down (`make audio-check D=<file>`). Mixed by internal/audio/audio.go; beds picked by core/audio-select.js. The CUES are synthesized and carry no licence (core/audio-kit.mjs), but the MUSIC beds under assets/music/ are downloaded third-party tracks — check assets/music/credits.json before any commercial release. See docs/CRAFT/SOUND.md.

music.label: Music bed. Silence is the default, so this is opt-in: "auto" (audio-select picks a bed by mood), a baked bed NAME (calm | warm | tense → assets/music/<name>.wav), or a path to a .wav. Omit for no bed. `make validate` resolves it against assets/music/ and the scene dir and warns if it will not.

auto.label: Auto-pick a music bed AND auto-derive sfx cues from cuts/stings (core/audio-select.js). Same as music:"auto".

musicGain.label: Music bed level (0 = muted, ~0.5 typical). Ducks automatically under VO.

musicDuck.label: Duck floor: how far the bed drops while VO plays (0..1, e.g. 0.15).

loudness.label: Integrated loudness target in LUFS (negative, e.g. -14 for social). Absent = peak-normalize only.

vo.label: Voice-over WAV path (resolved against the scene dir + repo root). A named-but-missing file fails `make validate` (the mixer would silently drop it).

voWords.label: VO word-timing sidecar JSON: [{ "w": "hello", "t": 1.2 }] — drives word captions.

sfxGain.label: Master multiplier over EVERY sfx cue (authored + auto-derived).

cues.label: Sound-effect cues, each { t, name, gain }. THIS is where cues live (the engine reads `audio.cues`); there is no top-level `sfx`.

name.label: Cue name: a synthesized cue (core/audio-kit.mjs CUES) or a baked alias (whoosh/reveal/click/pop, see scripts/media/audio-bake.mjs). `make validate` guards this list against the live CUES registry.

spectrum.label: Precomputed spectrum sidecar JSON for audio-reactive layers (layer `react:{}`).

silent.label: Render with NO audio track at all. A real device — a film can be better mute — but never a shrug: pair it with `_why`. A film with no sound and no stated reason is not silent by style, it is unfinished, and `make audio-check` says so.

_why.label: One sentence saying what the silence is DOING (e.g. "autoplays muted in-feed; the type carries it alone"). Required alongside `silent:true` by `make audio-check`. Same mechanism as `authoring._why`: waiving costs a sentence, and that cost is what turns a reflex back into a decision.
